relations.subject: sgw:role-cmd
relations.evidence: You can also use the Sync Function's [role()](sync-function/sync-function-api-role-cmd.md) function to assign users to roles programmatically.

relations.subject: sgw:role
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - promoted relation, already established for this exact deletion-cascade behavior in roles.json
relations.evidence: Removing a role effectively revokes access to the channel that role is associated with. This may mean users will lose access to required documents.

relations.subject: sgw:read-access-control
relations.evidence:
Dynamically via Sync Function  
Programmatically within the sync function using the exposed helper function access() — see [Sync Function API](sync-function/sync-function-api.md)

relations.subject: sgw:write-access-control
relations.evidence: Do this using any combination of: [requireUser()](sync-function/sync-function-api-require-user-cmd.md), [requireRole()](sync-function/sync-function-api-require-role-cmd.md) or [requireAccess()](sync-function/sync-function-api-require-access-cmd.md).

relations.subject: sgw:admin-rest-api
relations.evidence: Note that when sending a change to Sync Gateway through the Admin REST API, the Sync Function executes with admin privileges. Calls to `requireUser`, `requireAccess` and `requireRole` will be no-ops, and will always appear successful.

relations.subject: sgw:channel-cmd
relations.evidence: Here we are using a specific XATTR to determine which users need access to the document's contents — for more on how to configure ths see [Use XATTRs for Access Grants](access-control-how-use-xattrs-for-access-grants.md).

relations.subject: sgw:access-cmd
relations.evidence: The access() function can also operate on roles. If a user name string begins with role: then the remainder of the string is interpreted as a role name.

notable_absence.finding: Restated identically to access-control-how-control-document-access.json's finding, with this page's own quote: 'Channels enforce read access control to the documents. Any user who has access to a document can update the document.' Write access is fail-open by default in Sync Gateway; the only narrowing mechanism is hand-authored requireUser()/requireRole()/requireAccess() calls inside the sync function, none of which are enforced by the platform unless the docs author writes them, and all of which are unconditionally bypassed for calls made through the Admin REST API.

cross_component_finding: This page is a composite/merged index that reproduces, verbatim and in full, the content of four already-separately-extracted round-3 pages (access-control-how-create-users.md, access-control-how-create-roles.md, access-control-how-assign-users-to-roles.md, access-control-how-control-document-access.md) PLUS the entire content of this round's access-control-how-verify-access.md and access-control-how-use-xattrs-for-access-grants.md sections, all concatenated under one URL with anchored sub-headings (#lbl-acc-ctl-users, #lbl-acc-ctl-roles-create, #lbl-control-document-access, #lbl-verify-access, #lbl-xattrs). This looks like an Antora/AsciiDoc composite page assembled via include directives, rendered here as one flat markdown file alongside separately-rendered child pages carrying identical prose. Flagging for the coordinator: every relation captured here duplicates a relation already recorded (in this batch or round 3) against a different page_id for the identical sentence - a five-way content duplication (this page + 5 children) is a stronger version of the sync-function.json/sync-function-api-require-role-cmd.json duplication already noted in round 3's own finding. Reconciliation should treat this page_id as a low-priority alias-source rather than independent corroborating evidence when computing concept/relation recurrence counts.
cross_product_finding: One page-local detail worth surfacing again in full: the 'Ways to configure access' list treats the Legacy Pre-3.0 config file, the Admin REST API's admin_channel field, and the Sync Function's access() call as three textually equal, interchangeable provisioning surfaces for the identical grantsChannelAccess relationship - there is no single canonical grant path the way a Capella role assignment or a Server RBAC GRANT statement is centralized through one mechanism. Example 1's caption ('Documents are assigned to channel using the Sync Function's channel() API' / 'User and-or roles are granted access to channels by one of the means defined in Ways to configure access') is the single clearest visual statement in the whole corpus of SGW's two-control-point model: one call (channel()) tags documents, a structurally unrelated set of calls/fields (admin_channels, access()) tags identities, and read access is the set-intersection of the two - reconfirming round 3's headline finding against this page's own independent restatement of it.
